speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing generalized fatigue, severe pruritus, and abnormal liver function tests. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any specific changes in your skin, such as jaundice or a rash, or any changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of ulcerative colitis and risky sexual behavior, I need to know if you have noticed dark urine or pale, clay-colored stools, which could indicate bile duct obstruction. Additionally, have you experienced any fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss?

REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (focusing on Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase, ALT, AST)
REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C antibody, and HIV 1/2 Ag/Ab
REQUEST TEST: RPR (Syphilis serology)
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin_Total: 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 460 U/L, AST: 75 U/L, ALT: 78 U/L; Hepatitis B surface antigen: Not Provided, Hepatitis C antibody: Not Provided, HIV 1/2 Ag/Ab: Not Provided, RPR: Not Provided; Abdominal_Ultrasound: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.

The combination of your history of ulcerative colitis, the ultrasound showing thickening and focal dilatation of the bile ducts ("beads on a string"), and the cholestatic liver enzyme pattern (elevated Alkaline Phosphatase with normal bilirubin) strongly supports this diagnosis. Do you have a family history of this condition or autoimmune diseases like primary biliary cholangitis?
